# Unreleased

Staging note for the next release. Fold it into that release's `<tag>.md` (the release job reads `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`) and delete this file.

## New

- `--policy` takes a file: a path (`./ci/policy.yaml`, `~/policy.yaml`, anything ending in `.yaml` or `.yml`) is read in the `permissions.yaml` format, and its levels and settings stand in for your own for the run.
- A `web:` section in `config.yaml` configures how pages are fetched: an off switch, the User-Agent (a `continuous` product token by default, a generic string, a custom one, or a Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari preset), `robots.txt` handling (`ask`, `respect`, `ignore`), HTTPS only, byte, time, redirect, rate and character limits, the session cache, per-host headers and User-Agent, reputation providers, crawler politeness and the search backend. `web.limits.maxBytes` and `web.limits.timeoutSeconds` are in force now for the fetch tool and `@url`; the other keys are accepted and validated and take effect as the fetch work lands. Only your own config.yaml may loosen a web setting or set what is sent to sites; an assistant or a project folder may only tighten, and what it may not set is ignored with a notice. `toolPermissions.auto.environment.fetchMaxBytes` and `fetchTimeoutSeconds` still work, with a deprecation notice once per session and in `continuous doctor config`. See "Web fetch and URLs" in the docs, which also lists every path that fetches and what each one sends.
- Every fetched page (the fetch tool, `Fetch` in `cn`, and `@url`) starts with one provenance line: final URL, status, size, time, SHA-256 prefix, `robots.txt` verdict (not checked yet) and the rule that allowed it. Every web request, refused ones included, goes to an in-memory fetch log for the session and to the audit trail as a `fetch` line with query values masked.
- Changing tools while the prompt cache is warm no longer rebuilds the cache without asking. Turning a tool, a tool group or an MCP server on or off, or a server that connects late or changes its tools, now waits until the cache goes cold when re-reading the conversation would cost a significant amount. The Tools page says what applying it now would cost and offers Apply now, Apply when the cache goes cold (the default) or Start a new session with it; a line above the input shows what is waiting. In the `cn` command line, `/tools` lists waiting changes and `/tools apply` applies them. See "Changing tools during a session" in the prompt caching docs.

## Behaviour changes

- **Breaking change for scripts: headless runs no longer allow everything.** `cn -p` and `cn serve` now run at your own policy levels (the ones saved in `permissions.yaml`, or the defaults, Careful) with the same lists as the terminal UI, so `Bash`, edits and MCP tools ask, and a call that would ask is refused because nobody can answer it. The model gets a tool result that says why, stderr gets one line per refused tool naming the flags that allow it, and every headless run starts with one stderr line naming its levels. A read-only command (Context use Permissive) and anything a rule allows still run; at IDGAF (`--policy idgaf` or `--auto`) everything runs. Before, the headless lists allowed `Bash` and every unlisted tool, MCP tools included. Migration: add `--auto` (everything, as before) or `--policy handsOff` (commands and edits run, a dependency change or other always-ask call is still refused) to the command, or `--policy ./policy.yaml` for levels kept in a file; `CONTINUOUS_HEADLESS_LEGACY_ALLOW=1` restores the old lists for this release only and is removed in the next.

- Add model > CometAPI no longer offers Claude Sonnet 4.5 (retires 2026-11-30; CometAPI has no Sonnet 5.5 preset yet) or the retired Claude Opus 4.1, Claude Opus 4.1 Thinking, Claude Sonnet 4, Claude Sonnet 4 Thinking and Claude 3.7 Sonnet Latest; Claude Haiku 4.5 stays. Existing configs and pricing are unchanged.
- Prompt cache, once: the first request after upgrading writes the prompt cache once because the prompt prefix changed. The changes are all in text sent to the model: the `multi_edit` / `MultiEdit` tool description is shorter (the same rules in about a quarter of the words), the terminal agent's git status in the environment block is capped at 40 files and 4,000 characters (the rest is counted in a "... and N more changed files" line, files listed by path), and, with tool search on, the `search_tools` description now lists every deferrable tool and no longer changes after a search. Tool search is still off by default. In the terminal agent the tools a search activated are now read from the conversation, so a resumed session keeps the tools its history already called and a new session in the same process starts with none.
- A tool turned off while the prompt cache is warm stays in the request's tool list until the cache goes cold, after compaction or in a new session, and a call to it is refused with a result that says why and recorded in the audit trail. To apply tool changes at once as before, choose "Apply tool changes at once" in the prompt cache menu, or set `CONTINUE_TOOL_CHANGES=now` for `cn`.
- On models with preserved thinking's prefix check (Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, and depending on the account Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5), the reasoning from before a tool list change is no longer sent back once the change applies, because those models refuse it.

## Fixes

- **Security: `@url` followed redirects to private addresses and sent your gateway headers to any site.** A public page named with `@url` could redirect to the cloud metadata service (`169.254.169.254`) or another private or loopback address, and Continuous followed it (up to 20 hops) and gave the reply to the model. `@url` also sent every `requestOptions.headers` value, often a gateway or proxy token, to whatever site you named, and `@web`, the `search_web` tool and `@google` sent them to the search service. Now `@url`, the favicon lookup and the search paths go through the same guard as the fetch tool: at most five redirects, every hop checked again, a redirect to a non-public or link-local address refused, the connection pinned to the address that was checked (no DNS rebinding), and the global headers sent only to your model endpoints. Upgrade if you use `@url` on a machine that can reach a metadata service or an internal network, or if your `requestOptions.headers` carry a credential.
- The fetch guard now treats every IANA special-purpose block that is not globally reachable as private (documentation, benchmarking, `192.0.0.0/24`, `2001:db8::/32`, `100::/64` and others, from the registry itself), refuses a redirect whose address carries a credential, and drops `Authorization` and `Cookie` when a redirect changes origin.
- Favicons must be raster images of at most 256 KiB, fetched within 5 seconds; an SVG icon is no longer embedded. The search response is capped at the fetch size limit with a deadline, and search and fetch errors give the HTTP status without quoting the response body.

- An unsent message no longer comes back with the "Restored your unsent message" notice after a trip to Settings (or another page of the panel) and back; the text returns quietly. The notice still shows after a window reload, an extension update or a crash, and when you return to a session after opening another.
- **Open the Audit Inbox** lands on the Inbox each time it runs, also after you switched the Permissions page to another view by hand.
- Settings > Providers says how an AWS profile signs in: SSO, `credential_process`, an assumed role, a web identity token, or access keys in `~/.aws/config` or `~/.aws/credentials`. It reads only the key names in the profile's `~/.aws/config` section and never opens `~/.aws/credentials`.
- **No conversation starters while a session reopens.** A large session takes a while to arrive from the IDE, and the empty chat with its starters showed until then. The chat now says which session is loading and offers **Start a new session instead** and the recent sessions. Typing, a new session or opening another one drops the load, so it cannot replace what you started, and the text you typed stays in the input. Only a session this window reopens (one of its workspace) shows the view. A session that went to the trash or cannot be read opens as an empty chat with a short note, under a new id.
